outline: Title, metadata and abstract
State nonempty P, closure operations and principal conclusion.
Introduction
Conjecture, reduction to projections, comparison of related results, notation and source edition.
The Boolean proof category
Define formulas, operations, witnessed zeros, congruences and maximality; state main theorem.
Occurrences and substitution
Faithful relational interpretation, nonthinness, exponential obstruction, normal forms, signed literals and substitution maps.
Isolating an occurrence
Construct selected one-edge relations and transport the contextual equation by substitution, including negative literals.
Contextual collapse
Identify q/e, prove thinness and main theorem, then obtain the model corollary by universal agreement.
Lean formalization
State syntax/quotient correspondence, both proof routes and registered declaration family.
Appendix A.1: profiles and their fibres
Define labelled blocks, gamma and chi; prove square identities.
Appendix A.2: finite ordinals
Prefix sums, encoding bijections, block locator, skeleton/profile reconstruction and worked example.
Appendix A.3: shared variables
Renaming square and positive/negative contextual instances.
Appendix B
Typed diagrams of three defining equations.
Appendix C
Correct two source rank sentences and justify each correction.
Disclosure and bibliography
Preserve authorized disclosure and identify exact sources.

edits.why: Add the omitted cartesian-closed maximality antecedent, with its proof method and the obstruction to applying it here.
edits.old:
For cartesian categories, Do\v{s}en and Petri\'c prove maximality by
using coherence, substitution and composition to derive equality of
the product projections \cite[\S5]{DPCartesian}.
Sections~\ref{sec:isolation} and~\ref{sec:collapse} give the reduction
for the zero-identity Boolean category.
edits.new:
For cartesian categories, Do\v{s}en and Petri\'c prove maximality by
using coherence, substitution and composition to derive equality of
the product projections \cite[\S5]{DPCartesian}.
For cartesian closed categories, they obtain the same conclusion
from a typed B\"ohm theorem \cite[\S11]{DPCCC}.
The latter result does not apply to $\B$: the exponential
$p\Rightarrow p$ does not exist, as shown in
Section~\ref{sec:occurrences}. Sections~\ref{sec:isolation}
and~\ref{sec:collapse} give the reduction to equal projections in $\B$.

edits.why: Name the closest zero-identity distributive-lattice antecedents, verified on DP p.292.
edits.old:
Do\v{s}en and Petri\'c also prove maximality for lattice categories

edits.new:
Do\v{s}en and Petri\'c prove maximality for lattice categories
and relative maximality for dicartesian categories
\cite[\S\S8--10]{DPBicartesian}, without assuming distribution.
Their book proves maximality for zero-identity distributive lattice

edits.why: Restore the negation-free hypothesis of cited Lemma 6. Without it, p→(¬p∨p) and the negative target occurrence refute the unqualified description.
edits.old:
Their Lemma~6 in \cite{DPIsomorphic} constructs an arrow whose
relation links just two prescribed occurrences of the same variable,
provided the implication between its source and target is a tautology.
edits.new:
For formulas $A,B$ containing no negation, with $A\to B$ a
tautology, \cite[Lemma~6]{DPIsomorphic} constructs an arrow
$A\to B$ whose occurrence relation consists of the edge between
any prescribed occurrences of the same variable in $A$ and $B$.

edits.why: Add the authors' proof-net coherence result and identify its graph category, instead of treating every graphical semantics as Rel.
edits.old:
Other definitions of Boolean category start with monoidal operations
for conjunction and disjunction.
edits.new:
For multiplicative linear logic without constants, Do\v{s}en and
Petri\'c prove coherence for proof-net categories, with and without
mix, with respect to Brauerian split equivalences \cite{DPPN}.

Other definitions of Boolean category do not require conjunction and
disjunction to be categorical products and coproducts.

edits.why: State the collapse theorem in the exact initial-object/exponential form of the cited page; retain the independent obstruction for B.
edits.old:
Joyal's collapse theorem concerns cartesian closed categories with a
dualizing object; see \cite[\S14.3, pp.~324--326]{DP}. The category
$\B$ is not cartesian closed. Indeed, faithfulness gives at most one
arrow $\top\to E$ for every $E$, since $\Occ(\top)$ is empty,
whereas $1_p\ne0_p$. An exponential $p\Rightarrow p$ would give
a bijection $\B(p,p)\cong\B(\top,p\Rightarrow p)$, a contradiction.
edits.new:
Joyal's collapse result says that a cartesian closed category with
an initial object $\bot$ is a preorder if
$A\cong(A\Rightarrow\bot)\Rightarrow\bot$ for every object $A$
\cite[\S14.3, p.~324]{DP}.
The category $\B$ is not cartesian closed. Faithfulness gives at most
one arrow $\top\to E$ for every $E$, since $\Occ(\top)$ is empty,
whereas $1_p\ne0_p$ for $p\in P$. An exponential $p\Rightarrow p$
would give a bijection $\B(p,p)\cong\B(\top,p\Rightarrow p)$,
a contradiction.

edits.old:
The right-hand side is independent of $B$. The symmetry of mix gives
$h_A\circ\langle\pi_2^{A,A},\pi_1^{A,A}\rangle=h_A$.
Together with \eqref{eq:context} for all formulas, this identity yields

edits.new:
The right-hand side is independent of $B$. The symmetry of mix gives
$h_A\circ\langle\pi_2^{A,A},\pi_1^{A,A}\rangle=h_A$.
Write $\equiv$ for equality modulo a proof congruence containing \eqref{eq:context}
for every formula. Taking $B=\bot$ in the expression for mix,
\eqref{eq:context} and Boolean Coherence in $\B$ give
\[
 j_A\circ h_A\equiv j_A\circ\pi_2^{A,A}.
\]
Precomposing with the symmetry of $A\wedge A$ and using the
preceding identity for $h_A$ gives
$j_A\circ\pi_1^{A,A}\equiv j_A\circ\pi_2^{A,A}$.
Precompose this equation with $\langle1_A,0_A\rangle$. Since the
composite $j_A\circ0_A$ has empty occurrence relation, coherence gives
\[
 j_A\equiv\iota_2^{A,\top}\circ!_A.
\]
The coproduct equations then make $A\vee\top$ terminal in the
quotient. By symmetry,
$\iota_2^{\top,A}\equiv\iota_1^{\top,A}\circ!_A$.
Taking $B=\top$ in the expression for mix and using
\eqref{eq:first-injection} now gives $h_A\equiv\pi_1^{A,A}$.
The symmetry of $h_A$ yields $\pi_1^{A,A}\equiv\pi_2^{A,A}$,
and pairing equates any two parallel arrows.
